issues.title: lifecycle-state.json out of sync with plan frontmatter
issues.details: .agent-skills/lifecycle-state.json still shows currentPhase 'track-a-peer-review-retry-required' and nextAction 'Retry the failed external workflow-plan review for Track A before requesting or starting implementation,' while the plan's own frontmatter now reads status: ready-for-approval. A downstream agent or operator consulting the sidecar state (the documented source for 'next action') would be told to retry a review that this artifact claims is already resolved.
issues.suggested_fix: Update lifecycle-state.json's currentPhase/nextAction to reflect the resolved peer-review status before or at the moment the plan is approved, consistent with the plan's own Slice 5 instruction to keep plan status and lifecycle-state.json synchronized.

verification_gaps: No execution evidence (actual uv run pyright or pytest output) exists yet to confirm the scoped-pyright approach works in practice; that is expected at this plan-gate stage, not a defect.
lifecycle-state.json sync timing (before approval vs. at approval) is not specified anywhere.
recommended_fixes: Sync .agent-skills/lifecycle-state.json currentPhase/nextAction to match the plan's ready-for-approval status before treating Track A as unblocked for implementation.
workflow_compliance: Plan frontmatter includes required fields (title, kind, status, canonicality, created/updated, source_of_truth, related, tags) and correctly reflects the requested status transition to ready-for-approval.
Scope, out-of-scope, risks/stop-gates, acceptance criteria, and Definition of Done sections are all present and internally consistent with the pyright-scoping change.
Verify commands (pytest suites, combined regression command, uv run pyright) reference test files confirmed to exist in the repo and a pyright config confirmed present in pyproject.toml.
technical_reality: pyproject.toml [tool.pyright] scopes include=['graphify','tests'] with typeCheckingMode='basic', i.e. `uv run pyright` runs repo-wide by default, which is exactly the condition the plan's new scoping sentence is designed to handle.
tests/test_cli_semantic_fail_closed.py and tests/test_extract_cli.py exist in the repo, so the two focused verify commands target real files.

lifecycle-state.json's currentPhase/nextAction were last updated 2026-07-13 but still describe a pre-fix state ('peer-review-retry-required'), indicating it was not touched in the same edit that updated the plan frontmatter.
assumptions_to_verify: That 'investigate only new or changed findings attributable to this repair in touched files' will be operationally treated as a hard gate (must resolve or explicitly justify) rather than an optional advisory step during actual implementation.
That lifecycle-state.json will in fact be updated per the plan's own Slice 5 instruction once this round's findings are closed out.
verification_sufficiency: Sufficient for the narrow freshness-check scope requested: both specific claims (pyright scope wording, frontmatter status) were directly read and confirmed present and accurate in the current artifact.

Not sufficient to certify the broader plan's feasibility beyond this round's two targeted claims, since code files and companion plan docs were not re-reviewed this round (consistent with prior rounds presumably already covering that ground).
downstream_risks: A future agent reading lifecycle-state.json instead of the plan frontmatter could re-trigger an unnecessary peer-review retry, wasting a review cycle.

The 'investigate' wording for new/changed pyright findings has no explicit escalation path if an investigation surfaces a real regression; low risk since Slice 3 already requires not weakening assertions to force a pass, but worth operator awareness during implementation.
review.freeze_recommendation: Safe to freeze. Carry the remaining WARN/NOTE items as explicit follow-ups or implementation-time checks.
